ai.headline: Anthropic Claude Mythos: LLM-to-Exploit-Chain Capability Confirmed on ExploitBench
ai.body: Anthropic's restricted Mythos Preview model can chain vulnerability primitives into complete end-to-end attack chains, outperforming all other evaluated models on ExploitBench and ExploitGym benchmarks. Separately, Project Glasswing deployed Mythos Preview with ~50 partners to find 10,000+ high/critical-severity vulnerabilities across 1,000+ open-source projects at >90% true-positive rates. Partners include Cloudflare, Mozilla, Palo Alto Networks, Microsoft, Oracle, and major banks — shifting the security bottleneck from discovery to verification and patching.

ai.headline: Google DeepMind AlphaProof Nexus Solves Nine Open Erdős Problems
ai.body: AlphaProof Nexus autonomously solved nine open Erdős problems — two unsolved for 56 years — at a few hundred dollars per problem, pairing an LLM with the Lean proof assistant for machine-verified proofs. It also proved 44 open conjectures from OEIS; a simpler agent variant matched results but cost more, and problems requiring novel mathematical constructions remained unsolved. This follows OpenAI disproving an 80-year-old Erdős conjecture the prior week, marking a rapid escalation in AI mathematical reasoning.

ai.headline: MCP Specification Release Candidate Introduces Stateless Core
ai.body: The largest revision to the Model Context Protocol since launch is now in release candidate, introducing a stateless core designed for horizontal scale. This architectural shift has significant implications for agentic systems that rely on persistent server-side session state and will affect how MCP servers are deployed in enterprise and cloud environments.

ai.headline: DeepSeek Permanently Cuts V4 Pro Prices 75%, Undercuts All Frontier Models
ai.body: DeepSeek made its promotional 75% price cut on V4 Pro permanent, now sitting below OpenAI GPT-5, Anthropic Claude Opus 4.7, and Google Gemini 3.5 Flash. The gap is widest against frontier reasoning models used by enterprise for demanding workloads, intensifying margin pressure across the AI provider stack.

ai.headline: Anthropic Overtakes OpenAI in US Business Adoption; Market Remains Fluid
ai.body: Ramp spend data shows Claude is now used by 34.4% of US businesses vs OpenAI's 32.3% — the first time Anthropic has led. However, over half of customers use both providers and 43% of Anthropic users switched from a competitor, indicating switching costs remain near zero and no durable moat has formed.

sec.headline: CVE-2026-48172 (CVSS 10.0): LiteSpeed cPanel Plugin 0-Day Actively Exploited for Root Access
sec.body: A logic flaw in the LiteSpeed User-End cPanel plugin's lsws.redisAble JSON-API endpoint allows any authenticated cPanel user to escalate to root with a single malformed API call — no race condition required. Particularly dangerous on shared hosting where all tenants hold valid sessions; cPanel force-uninstalled the plugin five hours before scheduled disclosure. Patch to LiteSpeed WHM Plugin v5.3.1.0 (bundled with cPanel Plugin v2.4.7) immediately and treat any host with `/var/cpanel/logs` entries matching `cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble` as fully compromised.

sec.headline: Apple M5 Memory Integrity Enforcement Bypassed in 5 Days Using Mythos Preview
sec.body: A three-person team using Anthropic's Mythos Preview produced the first public macOS kernel exploit defeating Apple's Memory Integrity Enforcement on M5 silicon, chaining CVE-2026-28952 with an info leak to reach a root shell in five days. The root cause is an integer overflow in `_zalloc_ro_mut` — the sole trusted writer for read-only kernel zones — that spills attacker-controlled bytes across slot boundaries and flips cr_uid to zero without touching pointers, tags, or page tables. This reframes hardware memory tagging as shifting rather than eliminating the attack surface, with privileged writers now the highest-value target.

sec.headline: TeamPCP Supply Chain Campaign: 700+ GitHub Repos Poisoned via Postinstall Hook
sec.body: A coordinated campaign linked to the `parikhpreyash4` GitHub account inserted identical `package.json` postinstall hooks across 700+ repositories, including popular Packagist packages and GitHub Actions workflows, deploying a binary (`gvfsd-network` / `/tmp/.sshd`) via `curl -skL` with TLS verification disabled. The hook was placed in `package.json` rather than `composer.json` to evade PHP defenders, and a CI/CD path was targeted via a workflow step named 'Dependency Cache Sync'. GitHub itself was breached via a poisoned VSCode extension; the group appears financially motivated with ransomware and data extortion payloads.

sec.headline: Netherlands Seizes 800 Servers, Arrests Two for Hosting Russia-Linked Cyberattack Infrastructure
sec.body: Dutch financial crime agency FIOD arrested two men — MIRhosting founder Andrey Nesterenko and associate Youssef Zinad — for violating EU sanctions law by providing hosting infrastructure used by Russia for DDoS attacks, influence operations, and disinformation campaigns. The seized 800 servers belonged to the-hosting / WorkTitans BV, successor entities to EU-sanctioned PQHosting and the Neculiti brothers, which had transferred Stark Industries' network assets ahead of sanction enforcement. Data on seized servers was irrecoverably lost for customers.

sec.headline: npm Staged Publishing: 2FA-Gated Tarball Approval and Install-Time Source Controls
sec.body: GitHub is adding staged publishing to npm requiring maintainers to pass 2FA and explicitly approve a prebuilt tarball before any version becomes installable, including from CI/CD and OIDC trusted publishing. npm CLI 11.15.0 adds `--allow-file`, `--allow-remote`, and `--allow-directory` flags to allowlist non-registry install sources, directly addressing supply chain abuse vectors exploited in the TeamPCP campaign.

fin.headline: Plaid Launches Guaranteed ACH: Absorbs Payment Failure Risk with Real-Time Risk Models
fin.body: Plaid's new guaranteed ACH product instantly approves bank transfers while Plaid absorbs financial risk if payments fail, backed by proprietary real-time risk models for improved transaction categorisation and income detection. The move positions Plaid as core payment infrastructure rather than a connectivity layer, competing directly with card networks and traditional ACH risk providers. Combined with new AI data tools, this is a significant expansion of Plaid's addressable market.

fin.headline: Claude Deeply Embedded in Institutional Finance Workflows at PwC, JPMorgan, Goldman, Visa
fin.body: Anthropic has launched finance-focused Claude agents covering reconciliations, valuation reviews, earnings analysis, and statement audits, with Microsoft Office integration. Adoption is concentrated among firms with existing enterprise data connectors — PwC, KPMG, JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, Citi, AIG, and Visa are named. A UK government report separately warns AI could automate 30-50% of financial services tasks, with HSBC, Standard Chartered, and JPMorgan executives openly acknowledging headcount reduction in certain roles.

fin.headline: Blockchain.com Confidentially Files for US IPO Amid Crypto Industry Listing Wave
fin.body: Blockchain.com has confidentially filed for a US IPO, joining Kraken and Grayscale as crypto firms testing public markets following the 2025 downturn and advancing federal crypto legislation. Valuation and timing remain undisclosed. The wave signals that regulatory clarity is finally progressing enough for digital asset firms to pursue listings.

swe.headline: CockroachDB C-SPANN: Distributed Vector Index Stored as Native Table Data
swe.body: CockroachDB's C-SPANN builds a hierarchical K-means tree where each partition is stored as ordinary key-value rows within CockroachDB ranges, inheriting existing split, rebalance, caching, and multi-region machinery for free. This avoids the central coordinator, large in-memory caches, and sharding-hostile layouts that disqualify HNSW and IVF for distributed transactional systems. Trade-off: C-SPANN loses on pure latency to specialized in-memory vector DBs but wins on transactional consistency, real-time updates, and multi-tenant isolation.

swe.headline: auth.md: Machine-Readable Agent Registration Standard for OAuth Flows
swe.body: WorkOS's auth.md proposes a standardised Markdown file that tells AI agents how to register on behalf of users — which OAuth flows are supported, which scopes exist, and how to register — without human interaction. The agent's identity provider vouches for the user. This is an early attempt at a non-human identity registration standard relevant to agentic IAM architecture.

swe.headline: HBM Now 63% of AI Chip Component Cost, Up from 52% in Early 2024
swe.body: Epoch AI data shows high-bandwidth memory has risen from 52% to 63% of total AI chip component spending between early 2024 and late 2025, now the dominant cost driver. Tech companies are raising capex forecasts by billions to manage tight HBM supply chains. This has direct implications for NVDA and TSMC supply chain dynamics and AI infrastructure cost curves.

mkt.headline: Neocloud Boom: SpaceX/xAI Deal Signals $7.5T AI Buildout Creating $2.5T Addressable Opportunity
mkt.body: SpaceX acquired xAI's two Colossus data centers and immediately rented them to Anthropic for $15B/year — nearly doubling SpaceX's $18.7B total revenue from 23 years of rocketry in a single quarter. The broader AI infrastructure buildout is projected at $7.5T over 4.5 years (~5% of US GDP, comparable to the 1880s railroad boom); if neoclouds capture 20% of the $13.5T in value created, that's a $2.5T opportunity that hyperscalers alone cannot fill. Direct relevance for AMZN, MSFT, GOOGL capital allocation and NVDA/TSMC demand.

mkt.headline: Anthropic Launches Enterprise Consulting Arm via Fractional AI Acquisition, Backed by Blackstone and H&F
mkt.body: Anthropic's new enterprise services firm — backed by Blackstone, Hellman & Friedman, and other major investors — has made Fractional AI its operational centerpiece. The move mirrors OpenAI's deployment strategy: using consulting-style teams and PE distribution networks to embed models across thousands of mid-market companies. This accelerates enterprise Claude adoption outside the direct API path.

deepDives.why: Primary Anthropic research benchmarking Mythos Preview on ExploitBench/ExploitGym; directly quantifies how fast the bar for offensive exploit development is dropping and what that means for defensive security teams.

deepDives.title: Project Glasswing Initial Update — Anthropic
deepDives.why: Official Anthropic announcement of AI-assisted vulnerability discovery at scale across critical open-source and enterprise infrastructure; sets the baseline for AI-driven offensive/defensive security economics.

deepDives.title: C-SPANN: Real-Time Indexing for Billions of Vectors in CockroachDB
deepDives.why: Primary engineering post-mortem from CockroachDB on architectural trade-offs of embedding distributed vector search natively in a transactional SQL system — a staff-level systems design reference for anyone evaluating vector DB strategy.
